items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular geography YouTube Shorts channel counting down six surprising facts. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: brisk and curious, with natural emphasis, a beat of excitement on each 'Number ...', and a short comic pause before each punchline.
lines: Narrator
You knock through a wall at home... and find a lost city? In Turkey, someone did.
Narrator
That's number three. Six Turkey facts that sound fake... and number one isn't about Turkey.
Narrator
Number six. Istanbul sits on two continents. Work in Europe... sleep in Asia.
Narrator
And it's not even the capital. That's Ankara.
Narrator
Number five. Turkey owns a whole sea: Marmara. Entirely inside its borders, and often called the world's smallest sea.
Narrator
So why all this in one country? Hold that thought.
Narrator
Number four. Santa Claus is from Turkey. Kind of. Saint Nicholas was a bishop in Myra, today's Dem-reh.
Narrator
Number three. That wall? In nineteen sixty-three, the story goes, a man fixing his house broke through... and found a city.
Narrator
He just wanted a bigger kitchen.
Narrator
Deh-rin-koo-yoo. About eighty-five metres deep. Room for up to twenty thousand people... and their animals.
Narrator
Number two. Gerb-eck-lee Teh-peh. Stone pillars raised about eleven thousand five hundred years ago. Six thousand years before Stonehenge. Before writing.
Narrator
So why here? Where two continents meet, everything passes through. Even a bird's name.
Narrator
Number one. English named a bird after Turkey. Turks call it "hindi"... the Indian bird. And in Hindi? "Peru".
Narrator
And the bird? It's from America.
Narrator
Since twenty twenty-two, the UN doesn't even say Turkey. It's Tur-kee-yay.
Narrator
This is Bhoogol. Follow for more Geography Fun Facts.
